title: Variants of vision encoder
reading: The slide surveys five families of vision encoder pretraining, each shown as a schematic architecture diagram with a canonical paper: supervised learning (ViT, Dosovitskiy et al.), masked modeling (MAE, He et al.), auto-encoding (VQVAE, Van den Oord et al.), self-distillation (DINO, Caron et al.), and multimodal learning (CLIP, Radford et al.). An inset bar chart in the upper right compares how often each family is used as the vision encoder in multimodal LLMs.

visuals.description: Five side-by-side architecture schematics: ViT patch embedding + transformer encoder + MLP head; MAE masked patches through encoder/decoder to reconstruct target; VQVAE CNN encoder, codebook embedding space, CNN decoder; DINO student/teacher networks with softmax, centering, EMA and stop-gradient; CLIP text and image encoders forming an image-text similarity matrix.
visuals.assertion: Vision encoders differ mainly in their pretraining objective: label supervision, masked reconstruction, discrete-latent reconstruction, self-distillation between student/teacher views, and image-text contrastive alignment.

visuals.description: Inset bar chart titled 'Popularity of different vision encoders in Multimodal LLMs' with near-zero bars for Masked Modeling and Supervised Learning, a small bar for Auto-encoding (e.g., VQ-VAE), a medium bar for Self-Distillation (e.g., DINOv2), and a very tall bar for Multimodal Learning (e.g., CLIP).
visuals.assertion: CLIP-style multimodal-learned encoders dominate usage in multimodal LLMs, far ahead of DINOv2-style self-distillation and other approaches.

concepts.name: Supervised ViT
concepts.why_it_matters: Baseline vision transformer trained with class labels.

concepts.name: VQ-VAE auto-encoding
concepts.why_it_matters: Learns discrete latent codes via reconstruction.

concepts.name: Self-distillation (DINO)
concepts.why_it_matters: Student-teacher training yields strong semantic features without labels.

concepts.name: CLIP contrastive multimodal learning
concepts.why_it_matters: Language-aligned features make it the default encoder for MLLMs.
